title: moonlight-N3DS: game streaming on a handheld

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if your New Nintendo 3DS could show a game that's actually running on your PC? That's the idea behind moonlight-N3DS.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's a streaming client. Your PC runs the game, and sends the picture over the network using the GameStream protocol. The 3DS receives it and sends your button presses back. Think of the handheld as a small window onto a faster machine.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's his fork of an upstream project by zoeyjodon, where the community installs and discussion live, and which has around three hundred stars. His fork is where he tries out his own port experiments.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A C plus plus client that comes from the moonlight-embedded family, built for 3DS homebrew.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why the New 3DS and not the original?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The newer model has more RAM and CPU headroom, which is what a streaming client needs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a blog post on handheld streaming and homebrew, and the README on the n3ds-main branch, plus the moonlight-embedded wiki, covers getting started.
